body: - One deviation from G-Py-11 was found in the changed code.

- **G-Py-11 deviation**: `python/tests/lint/test_lint_doc_pointer_paths.py` line 694 uses a bare `# pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]` suppression without an inline reason. G-Py-11 requires every type suppression to carry an inline reason. The fix is to append a reason, for example: `# pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]  # accessing _REGISTRY to verify cli dispatch registration`.

- No other guideline deviations were found in the changed code. The new `lint_doc_pointer_paths.py` module correctly follows G-CLI-1 (module-level `main(argv)->int` registered by domain/verb in the cli.py table), G-Enf-1 (mechanical enforcement of a recurring doc drift pattern), G-Prevent-1 (the lint-module-manifest entry names the justified new host with issue #7296 and explains why no existing host can absorb the rule), G-Py-1 (`Finding` is a `frozen=True` dataclass), G-Py-4 (narrow `OSError, UnicodeDecodeError` catch with a documented degraded-path return), and G-Sec-4 (symlink rejection in `_open_required_doc` and root-escape check in `_path_escapes_root`). The `# noqa: S106` suppression in the linter source at `lint_doc_pointer_paths.py` line 398 carries a reason, conforming to G-Py-11. The SECURITY.md prose-reference sweeps align with G-Md-2 (renamed module paths swept in the same change).
